question: How many credits is the computer science minor and which courses does it require?
answer:
The Computer Science Minor (Minor) requires between 16 and 24 credits, including non-General Education prerequisites and excluding lab science course credits [2].

Its listed requirements are [1]:
- Group 1: Select 3 courses, at least 3 of: CMPS 130 SCI PROBLEM SOLVING-PYTHON; CMPS 147 COMPUTER SCIENCE I; CMPS 148 COMPUTER SCIENCE II; CMPS 220 ASSEMBLY LANGUAGE PROGRAMMING; CMPS 231 DATA STRUCTURES; CMPS 240 DATA ANALYTICS IN PYTHON; CMPS 285 MOBILE DEVELOPMENT; CMPS 305 CYBER SECURITY; CMPS 310 BIG DATA PROGRAMMING; CMPS 311 OPERATING SYSTEMS; CMPS 315 THE LINUX ENVIRONMENT; CMPS 320 MACHINE LEARNING; CMPS 327 NETWORK PROGRAMMING; CMPS 331 ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE; an unnamed catalog entry; CMPS 337 COMPUTER VISION; CMPS 342 COMPUTER GRAPHICS; CMPS 345 ANALYSIS OF ALGORITHMS; CMPS 350 FINANCIAL MODELING; CMPS 357 THE .NET ENVIRONMENT; CMPS 361 SOFTWARE DESIGN; CMPS 364 DATABASE DESIGN; CMPS 366 ORGANIZATION OF PROGRAMMING LANGUAGES; CMPS 369 WEB APPLICATION DEVELOPMENT; CMPS 370 CYBER AND NETWORK DEFENSE; CMPS 373 OBJECT ORIENTED PROGRAMMING; CMPS 450 SENIOR PROJECT.
- Group 2: Select 2 courses, at least 2 of: CMPS 305 CYBER SECURITY; CMPS 310 BIG DATA PROGRAMMING; CMPS 311 OPERATING SYSTEMS; CMPS 315 THE LINUX ENVIRONMENT; CMPS 320 MACHINE LEARNING; CMPS 327 NETWORK PROGRAMMING; CMPS 331 ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE; an unnamed catalog entry; CMPS 337 COMPUTER VISION; CMPS 342 COMPUTER GRAPHICS; CMPS 345 ANALYSIS OF ALGORITHMS; CMPS 350 FINANCIAL MODELING; CMPS 357 THE .NET ENVIRONMENT; CMPS 361 SOFTWARE DESIGN; CMPS 364 DATABASE DESIGN; CMPS 366 ORGANIZATION OF PROGRAMMING LANGUAGES; CMPS 369 WEB APPLICATION DEVELOPMENT; CMPS 370 CYBER AND NETWORK DEFENSE; CMPS 373 OBJECT ORIENTED PROGRAMMING; CMPS 450 SENIOR PROJECT.
Note: all 300-level courses have prerequisites. Two possible prerequisite sequences are Sequence 1: CMPS 147 + CMPS 148 + CMPS 231; Sequence 2: CMPS 130 + CMPS 240. All 300-level courses are available to students completing Sequence 1; a subset are available to students taking Sequence 2 [1].
Also published: Computer Science 4+1, Computer Science BS, and Computer Science MS.

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-MN-CMPS) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1)

question: I'm a junior in the data science major. Is there a recommended order for the upper level electives, and do I need calc 2 before the stats courses?
answer:
The Data Science BS plan is for students admitted during 2026–2027; it places DATA 301 and DATA 225 in third-year fall, MATH 370 (Applied Statistics) in third-year spring, CMPS 320 and a DATA Elective in fourth-year fall, and DATA 450 in fourth-year spring. It gives no recommended order among elective choices. The plan’s semester totals are: first-year fall 16, spring 16; second-year fall 16, spring 16; third-year fall 16, spring 16; fourth-year fall 16, spring 16. [1]
The major requires one 4-credit elective, chosen from CMPS 310, CMPS 331, CMPS 369, ECON 310, INFO 320, MATH 253, MATH 305, or MATH 390. [1] The pages don’t say whether Calc 2 is required before the statistics courses. [1–3]
For prerequisites, the Registrar says to “review the prerequisite requirements in Web Self Service” and check course descriptions there. [2] The course-prerequisite page says to select a subject to see prerequisites. [3] Registrar: reg@ramapo.edu; (201) 684-7695. [2]

question: can I double major in finance and information systems, and how many total credits would the two together need
answer:
Yes. Ramapo says undergraduates may pursue a second major [5]. With two majors, no more than half the courses may count toward both, and you must complete all writing-intensive courses required for the second major [4].

The Finance BS plan for students admitted during 2026-2027 lists 128 credits [1]. That is not a stated combined total for Finance and Information Systems: undergraduates must complete at least 128 credits, and specific degree programs may exceed that minimum [7]. The supplied pages do not give Information Systems requirements or a combined credit total, so I can’t verify how many credits the two together require.

question: Should I take organic chemistry or anatomy first if I want to apply to nursing, which one is easier
answer:

That is not organic chemistry: the listed pre-nursing science requirements include CHEM 111 and anatomy and physiology, not organic chemistry [3].
